0. 0.1This Indian FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 7 August 1967, after the draft finalized by the Hospital Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division Council. 0.2 The formulation of Indian Standards on hospital equipment has been taken up on the recommendations of the Advisory Committee for the Development of the Surgical Instruments, Equipment and Appliances, Government of India. 0.3 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on hospital furniture. Other Standards published so far are: IS : 4035-1967 IS : 4037-1967 Specification for trolleys, stretcher Specification for stretchers and stretcher carriers

0.4 In order to minimize the risk arising from static electricity, only antistatic castors have been specified' and the top of the trolley is required to be free from any insulating coating or finish. Other accessories are to be fitted to the trolley in such a manner as to maintain electrical continuity between metal to metal. 0.5 In preparing this standard, from the following standards: considerable assistance has been derived Chief patients, complete. Ministry of Defence, GovernBritish Standards

IND/GS/MBD/504( c ) Trolleys, Inspectorate of General Stores, ment of India. B.S. 1962 : 1953 Patients' Institution. trolleys

( fixed top ).

0.6 In some of the clauses of the standard, re&ence has been made to IS: 4033* and IS: 4034t which are under preparation. Until these standards are published, the rquirementa in such clauses shall be subject to agreement between the concerned parties. 0.7 This standard contains a clause which calls for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. The relevant clause is 5.2.

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

The sheet metal top shall be dished to a depth of not less than 37 and not more than 50 mm.
